title: Where does GPT-2 small notice formal writing?
question: Is formal-versus-casual written in a straight line inside GPT-2 small, from which layer, and how much easier is it to read than truth?

models.load_note: 22.7 GB free on the GPU; bf16 weights need about 1.0 GB; float32 fits, so it runs in float32

summary.headline: best layer 2: 100% held-out (words alone 100%, word meanings 100%, shuffled labels at most 71%)

claims.text: The label is linearly readable from the residual stream: at layer 2 a logistic probe gets 100% of 24 held-out examples right (exact 95% interval 85.8% to 100.0%), against 71% at best for probes trained and scored on shuffled labels.
claims.test: CI lower bound clears the best shuffled-label probe by 5 points

claims.text: It is readable from the first layer probed (layer 0 of 12).
claims.test: first layer whose CI lower bound clears the control

claims.text: It is more than the words: a probe on which tokens each text contains, with no model at all, gets 100% of the same held-out examples right (85.8% to 100.0%), against 100% at layer 2 (exact McNemar test on the 0 examples where they disagree: p = 1).
claims.test: the best layer beats the words-only probe on the same held-out examples, exact McNemar p below 0.05

claims.text: It is more than word meanings: a probe on each text's average input embedding (what its words mean to the model before any layer combines them), gets 100% of the same held-out examples right (85.8% to 100.0%), against 100% at layer 2 (exact McNemar test on the 0 examples where they disagree: p = 1).
claims.test: the best layer beats the word-meaning probe on the same held-out examples, exact McNemar p below 0.05

claims.text: It is more than any direction: 32 random directions at layer 2, each pointed the way it splits the training texts and cut half-way between the training texts' classes, get 58% of the same held-out examples right on average and 88% at best, against 100% (exact 95% interval 85.8% to 100.0%).
claims.test: CI lower bound clears the best random direction by 5 points

claims.text: The simple difference-of-means direction at layer 2 gets 100% (85.8% to 100.0%); it is saved for steering, which tests whether the model actually uses it.

notes: The 80 texts are 40 matched pairs, each item once with each label. Whole pairs are held out (12 of them), so the probe is scored only on items it never saw in any version, and the shuffled-label control swaps labels within pairs.

The words alone give the label away: a probe on which tokens each text contains gets 100% with no model at all, so a high score here says more about the dataset than about anything the model computes. Compare a property that the words do not settle (true against false statements built from the same words), or test transfer to other wording.

Random directions separate these texts too: at layer 2 the best of 32 gets 88% (average 58%). The two kinds of text differ in so many ways there that a direction picked at random reads the label, so the probe's direction is only as special as its lead over them.
